title: Boundary handles: transition overlaps, motion-blur shutter and global-time signals
note: Synthetic. Lists the function exercised, the input and the expected outcome; authored, not run. No number here is a measurement of real rendering, latency, memory or cost.

calls.case: s2 changed; seams s1->s2 crossfade and s2->s3 hard cut
s2 changed with both seams hard cuts and a score shutter of 180 degrees
s3 changed, its code reads a global-time signal, it starts at 6 s
s2 changed and its score names a particle simulation, no checkpoint; and with hybrid/checkpoints/s2.json
hosts s1,s2 at 0-4 s and 4-8 s; and a non-contiguous pair

expect: a crossfade forces a group_host unit over s1+s2 with a handle for the incoming side and the reason; the hard-cut side adds nothing
hard cuts only: scene_host, with a shutter handle noted (1 frame each side for the film-wide finish)
a global-time scene that does not start at 0 falls back to full_film with the reason
stateful effect without a checkpoint widens to the continuity group (or full_film when the group is the film); with a checkpoint it stays narrow
the group host keeps relative times (the earliest host moves to data-start 0, the next to 4) and the root lasts the span; a gap throws instead of rendering empty time
